key_insight: A pretrained LLM can bootstrap its own learning by generating an automated curriculum targeted at problems just beyond its current ability, using a teacher-student meta-RL loop to surface latent knowledge and escape training plateaus.
problem_solved: Reinforcement learning finetuning of large reasoning models stalls when initial success rates are very low and training signals are sparse; the paper addresses how to create useful training signal automatically when the model cannot yet solve available problems.
method: SOAR framework: maintain a teacher copy of the model that proposes problems/tasks aimed at the student’s current ability.
Meta-reinforcement learning trains the teacher to generate curricula that maximize student improvement — focusing on the "edge of learnability" where problems are solvable with small progress.
Iterative teacher–student loop uses student performance gains as reward to select and refine generated problems, surfacing latent knowledge into actionable training examples.
impact: Enables efficient self-directed finetuning of reasoning LLMs without extensive human-crafted curricula or dense supervision, helping practitioners overcome low-signal plateaus and improve sample efficiency for hard reasoning tasks.
visual_elements: Teacher–Student loop diagram showing a teacher model generating tasks, a student model learning, and feedback from student success guiding the teacher.
Staircase or frontier graphic labeled "edge of learnability" illustrating tasks increasing in difficulty and the curriculum focusing on the step just above current capability.
Performance curves comparing standard RL fine-tuning (flat plateau) vs SOAR (escape from plateau and rising accuracy over time).
Icon set: brain/gear for latent knowledge, target for curriculum selection, and reward signal for meta-RL feedback.
paper_title: Teaching Models to Teach Themselves: Reasoning at the Edge of Learnability
paper_authors: Shobhita Sundaram, John Quan, Ariel Kwiatkowski, Kartik Ahuja, Yann Ollivier
